source.text: כִּֽי־תֵ֭שֵׁב לִלְח֣וֹם אֶת־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל בִּ֥ין תָּ֝בִ֗ין אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what [is] before you,

en.L: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, \q consider carefully what [is] before you,
en.B: When you are seated at a ruler's table, \q take careful note of what is in front of you,
en.R: Suppose you are invited to eat with an important ruler. \q Pay close attention to what is set before you.

fr.L: Quand tu t’assieds pour manger avec un souverain, \q considère attentivement ce qui [est] devant toi,
fr.B: Quand tu prends place à la table d’un souverain, \q observe bien ce qui se trouve devant toi,
fr.R: Imagine qu’un chef important t’invite à manger. \q Fais très attention à ce qu’on met devant toi.

decisions.choice: what is before you: the food, or the host
decisions.reason: The words can mean the dishes set out or the powerful person across the table. Either way the guest must stay alert; verses 1–3 are one piece of advice. They belong to "the words of the wise" (22:17–24:22), a collection with close parallels in the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope, which also warns about eating in the presence of a great man.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ שַׂכִּ֣ין בְּלֹעֶ֑ךָ אִם־בַּ֖עַל נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will put a knife in your throat if [are] a master of appetite you.

en.L: and put a knife to your throat \q if you [are] a person of [great] appetite.
en.B: and if you have a big appetite, \q hold a knife to your own throat.
en.R: If you love to eat, hold yourself back, \q as if a knife were at your throat.

fr.L: et mets un couteau à ta gorge \q si tu [es] un homme de [grand] appétit.
fr.B: et si tu as un gros appétit, \q mets-toi un couteau sur la gorge.
fr.R: Si tu aimes manger, retiens-toi, \q comme si un couteau était posé sur ta gorge.

decisions.choice: a knife to your throat: restrain yourself sternly
decisions.reason: The picture is an overstatement: treat your own greed as an enemy to be stopped. The throat is the place of appetite (nephesh, in the next words, can mean both).

decisions.choice: "mettre un couteau à sa gorge" kept as the picture at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The image is strong in French too and says "restrain yourself sternly" (meaning decision m1). Readable keeps it as a comparison after the plain command, as the English Readable does.

source.text: אַל־תִּ֭תְאָולְמַטְעַמּוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝ה֗וּא לֶ֣חֶם כְּזָבִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not crave for his delicacies, and it [is] food of lies.

en.L: Do not crave {{gender:their|his}} delicacies, \q for it [is] food of lies.
en.B: Do not long for the ruler's fine dishes, \q for that food is deceptive.
en.R: Do not be greedy for his fancy food. \q It is not what it seems.

fr.L: Ne convoite pas ses mets délicats, \q car c’[est] un aliment de mensonge.
fr.B: Ne désire pas les plats raffinés du souverain, \q car cette nourriture est trompeuse.
fr.R: Ne sois pas gourmand de ses bons plats. \q Ils ne sont pas ce qu’ils paraissent.

decisions.choice: food of lies: a meal with a hidden purpose
decisions.reason: The rich meal may be meant to win the guest over or to test him. Its generosity is not to be trusted.

decisions.choice: "ses mets délicats" with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting on "ses", as the English "{their|his}"
decisions.reason: French "ses" says "his" and "their" (of one person) alike, so the English gender setting on the pronoun has nothing to change in French. As the French style guide sets, generic pronouns in French take no setting; this holds for these chapters.

source.text: אַל־תִּיגַ֥ע לְֽהַעֲשִׁ֑יר מִֽבִּינָתְךָ֥ חֲדָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not labor to gain riches; from your understanding cease.

en.L: Do not wear yourself out to gain riches; \q cease from your [own] understanding.
en.B: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; \q have the sense to stop.
en.R: Do not work yourself to death trying to get rich. \q Be wise enough to stop.

fr.L: Ne t’épuise pas à acquérir la richesse ; \q cesse [de t’appuyer] sur ta [propre] intelligence.
fr.B: Ne t’épuise pas à devenir riche ; \q aie la sagesse de t’arrêter.
fr.R: Ne te tue pas au travail pour devenir riche. \q Sois assez sage pour t’arrêter.

decisions.choice: cease from your understanding: stop, using good sense
alternatives: stop relying on your own cleverness
decisions.reason: The line may mean "in your wisdom, stop" or "stop trusting your own schemes for getting rich" (3:5, 7). Both warn against making wealth the goal of life.

decisions.choice: do not toil for riches: a teaching shared with Amenemope
decisions.reason: The Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope has a close parallel to verses 4–5, including riches that fly away like birds.

decisions.choice: "cesse [de t'appuyer] sur ta [propre] intelligence"
decisions.reason: French cannot say "cease from your understanding" without a verb after "cesse"; the bracketed words follow the reading the English Literal leaves open. The Balanced and Readable levels give the sense of meaning decision m1 (stop, using good sense).

source.text: הֲתָ֤עִיף עֵינֶ֥יךָ בּ֗וֹ וְֽאֵ֫ינֶ֥נּוּ כִּ֤י עָשֹׂ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֣וֹ כְנָפַ֑יִם כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר יָע֥וּף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Do you cause to fly your eyes on it, and it [is] not? For surely it makes for itself wings like an eagle [that] flies [to] the heavens.

en.L: Will you let your eyes fly to it, and it [is] gone? \q For it surely makes itself wings \q like an eagle [that] flies [toward] the sky.
en.B: Cast a glance at wealth, and it is gone; \q it grows wings \q and flies off to the sky like an eagle.
en.R: Money can disappear in the blink of an eye. \q It is like a bird that grows wings and flies away.

fr.L: Laisseras-tu tes yeux voler vers elle, et elle [n’est] plus ? \q Car sûrement elle se fait des ailes, \q comme un aigle [qui] s’envole [vers] le ciel.
fr.B: Pose un regard sur la richesse, et elle a disparu ; \q elle se donne des ailes \q et s’envole vers le ciel comme un aigle.
fr.R: L’argent peut disparaître en un clin d’œil. \q Il est comme un oiseau à qui poussent des ailes et qui s’envole.

decisions.choice: will you let your eyes fly, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: will your eyes fly (the written form)
decisions.reason: The two forms differ only in the verb's stem; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: flies, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: let your eyes fly to it, and it is gone: wealth vanishes in a glance
decisions.reason: The eyes fly to wealth, and wealth flies away. The bird (nesher) may be an eagle or a vulture.

decisions.choice: "elle" for the riches of verse 4 ("la richesse")
decisions.reason: Hebrew "it" points back to the wealth of verse 4. French "la richesse" is feminine, so the pronoun is "elle"; Readable names "l'argent" and says "il".

source.text: אַל־תִּלְחַ֗ם אֶת־לֶ֭חֶם רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְאַל־תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו לְמַטְעַמֹּתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not eat the food of [one] evil of eye, and do not crave for his delicacies,

en.L: Do not eat the food of [one with an] evil eye, \q and do not crave {{gender:their|his}} delicacies,
en.B: Do not eat at the table of a stingy host, \q and do not long for their fine food,
en.R: Do not eat at the table of a stingy person. \q Do not want their fancy food.

fr.L: Ne mange pas le pain de [celui qui a] l’œil mauvais, \q et ne convoite pas ses mets délicats,
fr.B: Ne mange pas à la table d’un hôte avare, \q et ne désire pas ses bons plats,
fr.R: Ne va pas manger chez quelqu’un qui est avare. \q Ne désire pas ses bons plats.

decisions.choice: evil of eye: stingy, grudging
decisions.reason: The "evil eye" is the opposite of the "good eye" of 22:9, the generous person (28:22).

decisions.choice: crave, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: "le pain de celui qui a l'œil mauvais"
alternatives: "la nourriture de l'homme à l'œil mauvais"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "bread" and the idiom "evil eye"; Balanced and Readable say "avare", stingy, as meaning decision m1 reads it.

source.text: כִּ֤י׀כְּמוֹ־שָׁעַ֥ר בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ כֶּ֫ן־ה֥וּא אֱכֹ֣ל וּ֭שְׁתֵה יֹ֣אמַר לָ֑ךְ וְ֝לִבּ֗וֹ בַּל־עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: For as he calculates in his soul, so [is] he. Eat and drink, he says to you, but his heart [is] not with you.

en.L: For as {{gender:they|he}} reckons within {{gender:themselves|himself}}, so [is] {{gender:that one|he}}. \q "Eat and drink," {{gender:they say|he says}} to you, \q but {{gender:their|his}} heart [is] not with you.
en.B: Such people are always counting the cost. \q "Eat and drink!" they say to you, \q but their heart is not with you.
en.R: That kind of person keeps track of every bite you take. \q They tell you, "Eat and drink!" \q But they do not mean it.

fr.L: Car comme il calcule en lui-même, ainsi [est]-il. \q « Mange et bois », te dit-il, \q mais son cœur n’[est] pas avec toi.
fr.B: Ce genre d’homme compte toujours ce que cela lui coûte. \q « Mange et bois ! » te dit-il, \q mais son cœur n’est pas avec toi.
fr.R: Ce genre de personne surveille chaque bouchée que tu prends. \q Elle te dit : « Mange et bois ! » \q Mais elle ne le pense pas.

decisions.choice: as he reckons within himself: he counts the cost
alternatives: as he thinks in his heart, so is he
like a hair in the throat
decisions.reason: The verb (shaar) occurs only here; a related word means a measure or price. The host calculates what the meal costs him. The ancient Greek translation reads the line differently, with a picture of someone swallowing a hair. The familiar saying "as he thinks in his heart, so is he" takes the line out of its setting.

decisions.choice: always counting the cost; keeps track of every bite
alternatives: as he reckons within himself, so is he
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the rare verb plainly.

decisions.choice: "ce genre d'homme compte toujours ce que cela lui coûte" (generic "homme", then "il")
decisions.reason: The English Balanced uses "such people ... they". In French a singular host reads more naturally against the singular "te dit-il" of the Hebrew; "homme" here is the stingy host of verse 6, read as anyone. Readable says "ce genre de personne ... elle", which is plainly inclusive.

source.text: פִּֽתְּךָ־אָכַ֥לְתָּ תְקִיאֶ֑נָּה וְ֝שִׁחַ֗תָּ דְּבָרֶ֥יךָ הַנְּעִימִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Your morsel [which] you have eaten you will vomit it up, and you will waste your pleasant words.

en.L: The morsel you have eaten you will vomit up, \q and you will waste your pleasant words.
en.B: You will throw up the little you have eaten \q and squander your gracious words.
en.R: You will feel sick about what you ate. \q All your polite thanks will be wasted.

fr.L: Le morceau que tu as mangé, tu le vomiras, \q et tu auras gaspillé tes paroles aimables.
fr.B: Tu rendras le peu que tu as mangé \q et tu auras perdu tes paroles aimables.
fr.R: Tu regretteras ce que tu as mangé. \q Tous tes remerciements polis seront perdus.

decisions.choice: vomit up ... waste your pleasant words: the meal turns sour
decisions.reason: Once the guest sees the host's real attitude, the food sickens him and his compliments were for nothing.

source.text: בְּאָזְנֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל אַל־תְּדַבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־יָ֝ב֗וּז לְשֵׂ֣כֶל מִלֶּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] ears of a fool do not speak, for he will despise the insight of your words.

en.L: Do not speak in [the] ears of a fool, \q for {{gender:they|he}} will despise the good sense of your words.
en.B: Do not talk to a fool, \q who will only scorn your wise words.
en.R: Do not waste your breath on a fool. \q A fool will laugh at your good advice.

fr.L: Aux oreilles d’un insensé ne parle pas, \q car il méprisera le bon sens de tes paroles.
fr.B: Ne parle pas à un insensé : \q il ne fera que mépriser tes sages paroles.
fr.R: Ne perds pas ta salive avec un insensé. \q Il se moquera de tes bons conseils.

decisions.choice: fool: the closed-minded fool (kesil)
decisions.reason: Compare 9:7–8 and 26:4; Matthew 7:6.

decisions.choice: "l'insensé" for *kesil* at every level, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As the terms note for Psalms and Proverbs sets. "Fou" in French today suggests mental illness; "insensé" says a person who will not use sense, which is what the Hebrew word describes.

source.text: אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם וּבִשְׂדֵ֥י יְ֝תוֹמִ֗ים אַל־תָּבֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not displace a boundary of antiquity, and into [the] fields of fatherless ones do not go,

en.L: Do not move an ancient boundary stone, \q and do not go into [the] fields of [the] fatherless,
en.B: Do not shift an ancient boundary marker \q or encroach on the fields of orphans,
en.R: Do not move the old stones that mark where a field ends. \q Do not take land that belongs to orphans.

fr.L: Ne déplace pas une borne antique, \q et dans les champs des orphelins n’entre pas,
fr.B: Ne déplace pas une ancienne borne \q et n’empiète pas sur les champs des orphelins,
fr.R: Ne déplace pas les vieilles pierres qui marquent la limite d’un champ. \q Ne prends pas la terre qui appartient à des orphelins.

decisions.choice: an ancient boundary: the stones marking a family's land
decisions.reason: Fields were marked by boundary stones, and moving them was theft (22:28; Deuteronomy 19:14; 27:17). The Instruction of Amenemope also forbids moving boundary markers and taking a widow's land.

decisions.choice: the fatherless: those with no one to defend their land
decisions.reason: Orphans and widows were easy targets because they had no man to defend them in court (15:25).

source.text: כִּֽי־גֹאֲלָ֥ם חָזָ֑ק הֽוּא־יָרִ֖יב אֶת־רִיבָ֣ם אִתָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: for their redeemer [is] strong; he will conduct their case against you.

en.L: for their Redeemer [is] strong; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will plead their case against you.
en.B: for their Defender is strong, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will argue their cause against you.
en.R: God is their protector, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is strong. \q He will take their side against you.

fr.L: car leur Rédempteur [est] fort ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} plaidera leur cause contre toi.
fr.B: car leur Défenseur est fort, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} défendra leur cause contre toi.
fr.R: Dieu est leur protecteur, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est fort. \q Il prendra leur parti contre toi.

decisions.choice: their Redeemer: God as the next of kin of the helpless
decisions.reason: The redeemer (goel) was the relative who bought back family land and defended its people (Leviticus 25:25; Ruth 4:4). The fatherless have no such relative, so the LORD takes the role himself (22:23; Jeremiah 50:34).

decisions.choice: Defender
decisions.reason: Balanced names the role the verse describes: one who takes up their case.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the Redeemer stands for here, as the verse sense requires (22:23).

decisions.choice: "Rédempteur" at Literal; "Défenseur" at Balanced, as the English
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *goel* is the next of kin who buys back land and defends a helpless relative (meaning decision m1). "Rédempteur" is the usual French word for this title of God; Balanced says what he does here.

source.text: הָבִ֣יאָה לַמּוּסָ֣ר לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝אָזְנֶ֗ךָ לְאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: Bring to discipline your heart, and your ear to words of knowledge.

en.L: Bring your heart to discipline, \q and your ear to words of knowledge.
en.B: Set your mind on instruction \q and your ears on words of knowledge.
en.R: Pay attention when you are taught. \q Listen carefully to wise words.

fr.L: Applique ton cœur à la discipline, \q et ton oreille aux paroles de connaissance.
fr.B: Applique ton esprit à l’instruction \q et tes oreilles aux paroles de connaissance.
fr.R: Sois attentif quand on t’enseigne. \q Écoute bien les paroles sages.

decisions.choice: bring your heart to discipline: a new call to listen
decisions.reason: Like 22:17, the verse opens a fresh section of the teacher's words.

decisions.choice: "l'instruction" and "ton esprit" at Balanced, as the English "instruction" and "mind"
decisions.reason: The terms note gives "la discipline" for *musar* at Literal and Balanced; here the English Balanced says "instruction" because the word is about being taught, and French follows it. Literal keeps "la discipline" and "ton cœur".

source.text: אַל־תִּמְנַ֣ע מִנַּ֣עַר מוּסָ֑ר כִּֽי־תַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַ֝שֵּׁ֗בֶט לֹ֣א יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not withhold from a youth discipline; if you strike him with the rod, he will not die.

en.L: Do not withhold discipline from a child; \q if you strike {{gender:them|him}} with the rod, {{gender:they|he}} will not die.
en.B: Do not hold back correction from a child; \q if you punish them with the rod, they will not die.
en.R: Do not be afraid to correct a child. \q Punishing them with the rod will not kill them.

fr.L: Ne refuse pas la discipline à un enfant ; \q si tu le frappes avec la verge, il ne mourra pas.
fr.B: Ne prive pas un enfant de correction ; \q si tu le punis avec le bâton, il n’en mourra pas.
fr.R: N’aie pas peur de corriger un enfant. \q Le punir avec le bâton ne le tuera pas.

decisions.choice: the rod: physical discipline
decisions.reason: The rod was the usual means of correcting a child in the ancient world (13:24; 22:15; 29:15). The point of the saying is that love corrects; the means belongs to its time and must be read in the light of all Scripture says about love and justice.

decisions.choice: he will not die: correction will not destroy him
alternatives: he will not die an early death
decisions.reason: The line answers a parent's fear that correction is too harsh. Verse 14 adds that discipline keeps the child from a worse death.

decisions.choice: "la verge" at Literal; "le bâton" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: "La verge" is the traditional word for a stick used to punish, and keeps the Literal close to the Hebrew *shevet*; "le bâton" is the ordinary modern word.

source.text: אַ֭תָּה בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט תַּכֶּ֑נּוּ וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּצִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: You with the rod you will strike him, and his life from Sheol you will deliver.

en.L: You, strike {{gender:them|him}} with the rod, \q and you will deliver {{gender:their|his}} life from Sheol.
en.B: Punish them with the rod yourself, \q and you will save their life from Sheol.
en.R: When you correct them, \q you are saving them from an early grave.

fr.L: Toi, frappe-le avec la verge, \q et tu délivreras son âme du Shéol.
fr.B: Punis-le toi-même avec le bâton, \q et tu sauveras sa vie du séjour des morts.
fr.R: Quand tu le corriges, \q tu le sauves d’une mort trop tôt.

decisions.choice: you ... from Sheol: correction saves from death
decisions.reason: The "you" is emphatic: the parent who corrects is the one who rescues. Sheol is the world of the dead; a life without correction ends there early (5:23; 19:18).

decisions.choice: "le Shéol" at Literal; "le séjour des morts" at Balanced
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for these books. Readable follows the English "early grave" with "une mort trop tôt".

source.text: בְּ֭נִי אִם־חָכַ֣ם לִבֶּ֑ךָ יִשְׂמַ֖ח לִבִּ֣י גַם־אָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: My son, if is wise your heart, will rejoice my heart, even I.

en.L: My son, if your heart is wise, \q my heart will rejoice, even mine.
en.B: My son, if you have a wise heart, \q then I myself will be glad at heart.
en.R: My son, if you become wise, \q I will be very happy.

fr.L: Mon fils, si ton cœur est sage, \q mon cœur se réjouira, moi aussi.
fr.B: Mon fils, si tu as un cœur sage, \q alors moi aussi, j’aurai le cœur joyeux.
fr.R: Mon fils, si tu deviens sage, \q je serai très heureux.

decisions.choice: even I: the father's own joy
decisions.reason: The added "I" stresses that the teacher himself is moved (10:1; 27:11).

decisions.choice: "Mon fils" at every level, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for *beni*: "mon fils" is the natural French address of a father to his son, and the book is framed as a father's teaching.

source.text: וְתַעְלֹ֥זְנָה כִלְיוֹתָ֑י בְּדַבֵּ֥ר שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יךָ מֵישָׁרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And my kidneys will rejoice when your lips speak upright [things].

en.L: And my inmost being will exult \q when your lips speak what is right.
en.B: I will be glad to the depths of my being \q when I hear you speak what is right.
en.R: I will be full of joy when I hear you say what is right.

fr.L: Et mes reins exulteront \q quand tes lèvres diront ce qui est droit.
fr.B: Je serai heureux au plus profond de moi \q quand je t’entendrai dire ce qui est juste.
fr.R: Je serai plein de joie quand je t’entendrai dire ce qui est juste.

decisions.choice: my kidneys: my inmost self
decisions.reason: The kidneys stood for the deepest feelings (Psalm 16:7; Jeremiah 12:2).

decisions.choice: "mes reins" at Literal
alternatives: "mon être intime" at Literal, as the English
decisions.reason: French has the old image of the "reins" as the hidden self ("sonder les reins et les cœurs"), so Literal can keep the Hebrew word; Balanced and Readable give the sense, "au plus profond de moi" (meaning decision m1).

source.text: אַל־יְקַנֵּ֣א לִ֭בְּךָ בַּֽחַטָּאִ֑ים כִּ֥י אִם־בְּיִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not let your heart be jealous of sinners, but [be] in the fear of YHWH all the day.

en.L: Do not let your heart envy sinners, \q but [continue] in the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the day.
en.B: Do not let your heart envy sinners; \q instead, live in the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all day long.
en.R: Do not be jealous of people who do wrong. \q Instead, always honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe.

fr.L: Que ton cœur n’envie pas les pécheurs, \q mais [reste] dans la crainte {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} tout le jour.
fr.B: Que ton cœur n’envie pas les pécheurs ; \q vis plutôt dans la crainte {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} toute la journée.
fr.R: Ne sois pas jaloux des gens qui font le mal. \q Honore plutôt toujours {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avec respect.

decisions.choice: but in the fear of the LORD: the verb is understood
decisions.reason: The second line has no verb; "be" or "continue" is implied (24:1, 19; Psalm 37:1).

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" with "Yahvé" as the divine-name setting, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms note sets: "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, like the English "the LORD"; "l'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the form a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: "honore ... le SEIGNEUR avec respect" for "the fear of the LORD" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: Readable says what the fear of the LORD is, deep respect, as the English Readable "honor ... with awe" does.

source.text: כִּ֭י אִם־יֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.

en.L: For surely there is a future, \q and your hope will not be cut off.
en.B: Surely there is a future for you, \q and your hope will not be cut off.
en.R: You really do have a future. \q What you hope for will happen.

fr.L: Car sûrement il y a un avenir, \q et ton espérance ne sera pas retranchée.
fr.B: Oui, il y a un avenir pour toi, \q et ton espérance ne sera pas anéantie.
fr.R: Tu as vraiment un avenir. \q Ce que tu espères arrivera.

decisions.choice: a future: a good outcome at the end
decisions.reason: The word (aharit) is the end or outcome of a life (24:14, 20). Sinners may prosper now, but the one who fears the LORD has the better end.

source.text: שְׁמַע־אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י וַחֲכָ֑ם וְאַשֵּׁ֖ר בַּדֶּ֣רֶךְ לִבֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Listen, you, my son, and be wise, and guide in the way your heart.

en.L: Listen, you, my son, and be wise, \q and direct your heart in the way.
en.B: Listen, my son, and become wise; \q set your heart straight on the way.
en.R: Listen, my son, and be wise. \q Keep your mind on the right way to live.

fr.L: Écoute, toi, mon fils, et sois sage, \q et dirige ton cœur dans le chemin.
fr.B: Écoute, mon fils, et deviens sage ; \q tiens ton cœur droit sur le chemin.
fr.R: Écoute, mon fils, et sois sage. \q Garde ton esprit tourné vers la bonne façon de vivre.

decisions.choice: direct your heart in the way: keep to the right path
decisions.reason: The verb (ishsher) means to go straight ahead (4:14; 9:6). "The way" is the way of wisdom.

source.text: אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְסֹֽבְאֵי־יָ֑יִן בְּזֹלֲלֵ֖י בָשָׂ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be among drinkers of wine, among gluttons of meat for themselves,

en.L: Do not be among drinkers of wine, \q among those who gorge themselves on meat,
en.B: Do not keep company with heavy drinkers of wine \q or with those who stuff themselves with meat,
en.R: Do not spend time with people who drink too much or eat too much.

fr.L: Ne sois pas parmi les buveurs de vin, \q parmi ceux qui se gavent de viande,
fr.B: Ne fréquente pas ceux qui boivent trop de vin \q ni ceux qui se bourrent de viande,
fr.R: Ne passe pas ton temps avec des gens qui boivent trop ou qui mangent trop.

decisions.choice: drunkard and glutton: the rebellious son of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The same pair describes the son who will not listen to his parents (Deuteronomy 21:20).

source.text: כִּי־סֹבֵ֣א וְ֭זוֹלֵל יִוָּרֵ֑שׁ וּ֝קְרָעִ֗ים תַּלְבִּ֥ישׁ נוּמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For a drunkard and a glutton will become poor, and drowsiness will clothe [in] rags.

en.L: For [the] drunkard and [the] glutton will become poor, \q and drowsiness will clothe [them in] rags.
en.B: For drunkards and gluttons will end up poor, \q and their drowsiness will dress them in rags.
en.R: People who drink and eat too much will become poor. \q They get lazy and end up in rags.

fr.L: Car [l’]ivrogne et [le] glouton deviendront pauvres, \q et la somnolence [les] vêtira de haillons.
fr.B: Car les ivrognes et les gloutons finiront pauvres, \q et leur somnolence les habillera de haillons.
fr.R: Les gens qui boivent et mangent trop deviendront pauvres. \q Ils deviennent paresseux et finissent en haillons.

decisions.choice: drowsiness: the sleepiness that follows feasting
decisions.reason: The dullness after too much food and drink leads to laziness and so to poverty (6:9–11).

source.text: שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי־זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Listen to your father who begot you, and do not despise when she is old your mother.

en.L: Listen to your father who gave you life, \q and do not despise your mother when she is old.
en.B: Listen to the father who gave you life, \q and do not look down on your mother when she is old.
en.R: Listen to your father, who gave you life. \q Do not look down on your mother when she grows old.

fr.L: Écoute ton père qui t’a donné la vie, \q et ne méprise pas ta mère quand elle est vieille.
fr.B: Écoute le père qui t’a donné la vie, \q et ne regarde pas ta mère de haut quand elle a vieilli.
fr.R: Écoute ton père, qui t’a donné la vie. \q Ne méprise pas ta mère quand elle devient vieille.

decisions.choice: honor father and mother: as in the commandment
decisions.reason: Compare Exodus 20:12; Proverbs 1:8; 19:26; 30:17.

source.text: אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל־תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Truth buy and do not sell, wisdom and discipline and understanding.

en.L: Buy truth and do not sell [it]; \q [buy] wisdom and discipline and understanding.
en.B: Buy the truth and never sell it; \q get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
en.R: Truth is worth paying for, so get it and never give it up. \q Do the same with wisdom, correction, and understanding.

fr.L: Achète la vérité et ne [la] vends pas ; \q [achète] la sagesse, la discipline et l’intelligence.
fr.B: Achète la vérité et ne la vends jamais ; \q acquiers la sagesse, la discipline et l’intelligence.
fr.R: La vérité vaut la peine qu’on paie pour elle : obtiens-la et ne l’abandonne jamais. \q Fais de même avec la sagesse, la correction et l’intelligence.

decisions.choice: buy ... do not sell: gain at any cost and never give up
decisions.reason: As in 4:5, 7, wisdom is something to acquire like a valuable possession.

decisions.choice: "la discipline" (Literal, Balanced), "la correction" (Readable); "l'intelligence" for *binah*, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for *musar* and *binah*, so that the key words of Proverbs stay the same across chapters.

source.text: גִּ֣יל יָ֭גִיל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק וְיוֹלֵ֥ד חָ֝כָ֗ם יִשְׂמַח־בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Greatly rejoices [the] father of a righteous [son], and [one who] begets a wise [son] he rejoices in him.

en.L: [The] father of a righteous [son] will greatly rejoice, \q and [one who] fathers a wise [son] will be glad in him.
en.B: The father of a righteous son will be full of joy; \q a man who has a wise son will delight in him.
en.R: A father is very happy when his son does what is right. \q He is proud when his son is wise.

fr.L: Le père d’un [fils] juste exultera grandement, \q et [celui qui] engendre un [fils] sage se réjouira en lui.
fr.B: Le père d’un fils juste sera rempli de joie ; \q celui qui a un fils sage fera de lui sa joie.
fr.R: Un père est très heureux quand son fils fait ce qui est juste. \q Il est fier quand son fils est sage.

decisions.choice: greatly rejoices ... and one who fathers ... will be glad, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: the written form, spelled differently and without "and"
decisions.reason: The scribes' reading differs in the spelling of the verbs and adds "and" before the second line. The sense is the same.

source.text: יִֽשְׂמַח־אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: May your father and your mother rejoice, and may she rejoice, the [one who] bore you.

en.L: May your father and your mother be glad, \q and may she who bore you rejoice.
en.B: Let your father and mother be glad; \q let her who gave birth to you rejoice.
en.R: So make your father and mother happy. \q Bring joy to the mother who gave birth to you.

fr.L: Que ton père et ta mère se réjouissent, \q et qu’elle exulte, celle qui t’a enfanté.
fr.B: Que ton père et ta mère soient dans la joie ; \q qu’elle se réjouisse, celle qui t’a mis au monde.
fr.R: Rends donc ton père et ta mère heureux. \q Donne de la joie à la mère qui t’a mis au monde.

decisions.choice: may they rejoice: a wish that is also a call to the son
decisions.reason: The son can bring this joy about by living wisely (verse 24; 10:1).

source.text: תְּנָֽה־בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י תִּצֹּֽרְנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Give, my son, your heart to me, and your eyes my ways let them observe.

en.L: My son, give me your heart, \q and let your eyes observe my ways.
en.B: Give me your heart, my son, \q and let your eyes watch my ways.
en.R: My son, pay attention to me. \q Watch how I live and follow my example.

fr.L: Mon fils, donne-moi ton cœur, \q et que tes yeux observent mes voies.
fr.B: Donne-moi ton cœur, mon fils, \q et que tes yeux suivent mes chemins.
fr.R: Mon fils, écoute-moi bien. \q Regarde comment je vis et suis mon exemple.

decisions.choice: let your eyes observe, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: let your eyes delight in (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written form has a different verb: "let your eyes take pleasure in my ways."

decisions.choice: give me your heart: the father speaks, warning of the prostitute
decisions.reason: The appeal leads into the warning of verses 27–28, as in chapters 5–7.

source.text: כִּֽי־שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲמֻקָּ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וּבְאֵ֥ר צָ֝רָ֗ה נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For a deep pit [is] a prostitute, and a narrow well [is] a foreign [woman].

en.L: For a prostitute [is] a deep pit, \q and a foreign woman [is] a narrow well.
en.B: A prostitute is a deep pit; \q a foreign woman is a narrow well.
en.R: A prostitute is like a deep pit you fall into. \q A woman who belongs to another man is like a narrow well you cannot climb out of.

fr.L: Car une prostituée [est] une fosse profonde, \q et une étrangère [est] un puits étroit.
fr.B: La prostituée est une fosse profonde ; \q la femme étrangère est un puits étroit.
fr.R: Une prostituée est comme un trou profond où l’on tombe. \q La femme d’un autre est comme un puits étroit d’où l’on ne peut pas remonter.

decisions.choice: a prostitute ... a foreign woman: the woman of chapters 5–7
decisions.reason: The foreign woman (nokhriyyah) is the woman outside one's marriage (2:16; 5:20; 7:5). A pit and a narrow well are traps with no way out (22:14).

decisions.choice: a woman who belongs to another man
decisions.reason: Readable explains whom the foreign woman stands for, as in chapter 7.

decisions.choice: "une étrangère" (Literal), "la femme étrangère" (Balanced), "la femme d'un autre" (Readable)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for the strange or foreign woman, following each English level.

source.text: אַף־הִ֭יא כְּחֶ֣תֶף תֶּֽאֱרֹ֑ב וּ֝בוֹגְדִ֗ים בְּאָדָ֥ם תּוֹסִֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: Also she like a robber lies in wait, and the treacherous among humankind she increases.

en.L: She also lies in wait like a robber, \q and increases the treacherous among people.
en.B: She lies in wait like a robber \q and makes many men unfaithful.
en.R: She waits to catch men, like a robber. \q Because of her, many men break their promises to their wives.

fr.L: Elle aussi, comme un brigand, elle guette, \q et elle multiplie les infidèles parmi les humains.
fr.B: Elle se tient en embuscade comme un voleur \q et rend beaucoup d’hommes infidèles.
fr.R: Elle attend les hommes pour les attraper, comme un voleur. \q À cause d’elle, beaucoup d’hommes trahissent la promesse faite à leur femme.

decisions.choice: increases the treacherous: she makes men unfaithful
decisions.reason: Those she catches betray their wives and their vows (2:17). The word for robber (hetef) occurs only here.

source.text: לְמִ֨י א֥וֹי לְמִ֪י אֲב֡וֹי לְמִ֤י מִדְיָנִ֨ים׀לְמִ֥י שִׂ֗יחַ לְ֭מִי פְּצָעִ֣ים חִנָּ֑ם לְ֝מִ֗י חַכְלִל֥וּת עֵינָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: To whom [is] woe? To whom [is] sorrow? To whom [are] contentions? To whom [is] complaint? To whom [are] bruises without cause? To whom [is] dullness of eyes?

en.L: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has quarrels? Who has complaining? \q Who has wounds without cause? \q Who has dullness of eyes?
en.B: Who has trouble? Who has misery? Who is always fighting? Who is always complaining? \q Who has bruises for no reason? \q Who has bloodshot eyes?
en.R: Who is in trouble? Who is miserable? Who is always fighting and complaining? \q Who gets hurt for no reason? \q Whose eyes are red and blurry?

fr.L: À qui le malheur ? À qui la douleur ? À qui les querelles ? À qui la plainte ? \q À qui les blessures sans cause ? \q À qui l’obscurcissement des yeux ?
fr.B: Pour qui les ennuis ? Pour qui la misère ? Qui se dispute sans cesse ? Qui se plaint sans cesse ? \q Qui a des bleus sans raison ? \q Qui a les yeux injectés de sang ?
fr.R: Qui a des ennuis ? Qui est malheureux ? Qui se dispute et se plaint tout le temps ? \q Qui se fait mal sans raison ? \q Qui a les yeux rouges et troubles ?

decisions.choice: who has woe: a riddle that opens a poem on drunkenness
decisions.reason: Verses 29–35 form one poem. Six questions are answered in verse 30; the teacher then speaks to the listener, and the poem ends in the drinker's own words.

decisions.choice: quarrels, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: dullness of eyes: eyes dull or red from wine
decisions.reason: The word (hakhlilut) occurs only here; a related word is used of eyes darkened with wine in Genesis 49:12.

decisions.choice: "À qui le malheur ?" for "Who has woe?"
decisions.reason: French "à qui" with a noun is the natural form of this riddle and keeps the Hebrew "to whom"; Balanced moves to fuller questions.

source.text: לַֽמְאַחֲרִ֥ים עַל־הַיָּ֑יִן לַ֝בָּאִ֗ים לַחְקֹ֥ר מִמְסָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: To those who delay over the wine, to those who go to examine mixed wine.

en.L: Those who linger over the wine, \q those who go to taste mixed wine.
en.B: Those who stay up late over wine, \q who go looking for spiced drinks.
en.R: It is people who drink wine late into the night. \q They keep trying different kinds of strong drink.

fr.L: Ceux qui s’attardent auprès du vin, \q ceux qui vont goûter le vin mêlé.
fr.B: Ceux qui veillent tard autour du vin, \q qui vont chercher des boissons épicées.
fr.R: Ce sont ceux qui boivent du vin tard dans la nuit. \q Ils essaient sans cesse de nouvelles boissons fortes.

decisions.choice: mixed wine: wine blended with spices
decisions.reason: Wine was mixed with spices or herbs to make it stronger and richer (9:2; Isaiah 5:22).

source.text: אַל־תֵּ֥רֶא יַיִן֮ כִּ֪י יִתְאַ֫דָּ֥ם כִּֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן בַּכּ֣וֹס עֵינ֑וֹ יִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not look [at] wine when it is red, when it gives in the cup its eye, [when] it goes with smoothness.

en.L: Do not look [at] wine when it is red, \q when it gives its sparkle in the cup, \q [when] it goes down smoothly.
en.B: Do not gaze at the red wine \q as it gleams in the cup \q and slides down so easily.
en.R: Do not stare at red wine sparkling in a cup. \q It goes down easily.

fr.L: Ne regarde pas le vin quand il est rouge, \q quand il donne son éclat dans la coupe, \q [quand] il descend doucement.
fr.B: Ne fixe pas le vin rouge \q qui brille dans la coupe \q et qui coule si facilement.
fr.R: Ne regarde pas avec envie le vin rouge qui brille dans la coupe. \q Il se boit si facilement.

decisions.choice: in the cup, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written form can be read as "bag" or "purse"; the scribes' reading has "cup".

decisions.choice: gives its eye: sparkles, shows its gleam
decisions.reason: The "eye" of the wine is its glint or color in the cup.

decisions.choice: goes down smoothly
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of wine in Song of Songs 7:9.

source.text: אַ֭חֲרִיתוֹ כְּנָחָ֣שׁ יִשָּׁ֑ךְ וּֽכְצִפְעֹנִ֥י יַפְרִֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Its end like a snake it will bite, and like a viper it will sting.

en.L: At its end it bites like a snake \q and stings like a viper.
en.B: But at the last it bites like a snake \q and strikes like a viper.
en.R: But later it hurts you like the bite of a poisonous snake.

fr.L: À la fin, il mord comme un serpent \q et pique comme une vipère.
fr.B: Mais à la fin, il mord comme un serpent \q et frappe comme une vipère.
fr.R: Mais plus tard, il te fait du mal comme la morsure d’un serpent venimeux.

decisions.choice: viper: a poisonous snake
decisions.reason: The exact kind of snake (tsiphoni) is unknown (Isaiah 11:8). The verse turns from the pleasant start to the painful end (5:4).

source.text: עֵ֭ינֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּ זָר֑וֹת וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ יְדַבֵּ֥ר תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Your eyes will see strange [things], and your heart will speak perverse things.

en.L: Your eyes will see strange [things], \q and your heart will utter twisted things.
en.B: Your eyes will see strange sights, \q and your mind will say confused and twisted things.
en.R: You will see things that are not there. \q You will say things that make no sense.

fr.L: Tes yeux verront des [choses] étranges, \q et ton cœur dira des choses tordues.
fr.B: Tes yeux verront des choses étranges, \q et ton esprit dira des choses confuses et tordues.
fr.R: Tu verras des choses qui n’existent pas. \q Tu diras des choses qui n’ont pas de sens.

decisions.choice: strange things
decisions.reason: The word (zarot) is feminine plural and could mean "strange women", linking the poem to verses 27–28. More likely it refers to the drinker's confused sight.

source.text: וְ֭הָיִיתָ כְּשֹׁכֵ֣ב בְּלֶב־יָ֑ם וּ֝כְשֹׁכֵ֗ב בְּרֹ֣אשׁ חִבֵּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will be like [one who] lies down in [the] heart of [the] sea, and like [one who] lies down at [the] top of a mast.

en.L: And you will be like [one who] lies down in [the] heart of [the] sea, \q like [one who] lies down on [the] top of a mast.
en.B: You will be like someone sleeping in the middle of the sea, \q like someone lying at the top of a ship's mast.
en.R: You will feel dizzy, as if you were lying down on a ship far out at sea, \q or at the top of its tall pole.

fr.L: Et tu seras comme [celui qui] est couché au cœur de la mer, \q comme [celui qui] est couché au sommet d’un mât.
fr.B: Tu seras comme quelqu’un qui dort en pleine mer, \q comme quelqu’un d’allongé en haut du mât d’un navire.
fr.R: Tu auras la tête qui tourne, comme si tu étais couché sur un bateau loin en mer, \q ou en haut de son grand mât.

decisions.choice: the top of a mast: tossed and swaying
decisions.reason: The word (hibbel) occurs only here; it is related to the word for a sailor or ship's rope. The picture is the drunk's reeling head and his foolish ease in danger.

source.text: הִכּ֥וּנִי בַל־חָלִיתִי֮ הֲלָמ֗וּנִי בַּל־יָ֫דָ֥עְתִּי מָתַ֥י אָקִ֑יץ א֝וֹסִ֗יף אֲבַקְשֶׁ֥נּוּ עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: They struck me, not I am sick; they beat me, not I know. When will I awake? I will repeat [it]; I will seek it again.

en.L: [You will say,] "They struck me, [but] I was not hurt; \q they beat me, [but] I did not know [it]. \q When will I wake up? \q I will do it again; I will seek it once more."
en.B: "They hit me," you will say, "but I was not hurt; \q they beat me, but I did not feel it. \q When will I wake up? \q I will go and look for another drink."
en.R: You will say, "Someone hit me, but it did not hurt. \q They beat me, but I did not feel a thing. \q When will I wake up? I want another drink!"

fr.L: [Tu diras :] « On m’a frappé, [mais] je n’ai pas eu mal ; \q on m’a battu, [mais] je ne [l’]ai pas su. \q Quand me réveillerai-je ? \q Je recommencerai ; j’en redemanderai encore. »
fr.B: « On m’a frappé, diras-tu, mais je n’ai pas eu mal ; \q on m’a battu, mais je n’ai rien senti. \q Quand vais-je me réveiller ? \q J’irai chercher encore à boire. »
fr.R: Tu diras : « Quelqu’un m’a frappé, mais ça ne m’a pas fait mal. \q On m’a battu, mais je n’ai rien senti. \q Quand vais-je me réveiller ? Je veux encore boire ! »

decisions.choice: they struck me ... I will seek it again: the drinker speaks
decisions.reason: The poem ends in the drinker's own words. He does not feel the blows, and his first thought on waking is to drink again: wine has made him its slave.

decisions.choice: you will say
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves into the drinker's speech without a verb of saying; it is supplied to mark the quotation.

decisions.choice: another drink
alternatives: I will do it again; I will seek it once more
decisions.reason: "It" is the wine; Balanced and Readable say so.
